label: Pharmacy module
lead: Most hospitals run their attached pharmacy on a stand-alone billing software that doesn’t know what the doctor prescribed. Stock-outs surprise everyone. Dispensing errors compound. Lucoze’s pharmacy is part of the same record — prescription, dispense, stock, batch, all in one chain.

rows.title: Doctor prescribes. Pharmacy sees it instantly.
rows.lead: Prescription opens automatically at the pharmacy counter when the patient arrives. Out-of-stock substitutes are suggested with the doctor’s pre-approval. The patient counsel sheet prints in the local language.
bullets: Substitution rules at the prescription level — not the pharmacist’s discretion.
Patient counsel sheets in Hindi / Bengali / Odia with dosing instructions.
Refill reminders at 80% consumption — chronic-care patients don’t run out.

rows.title: Batches, expiry, reorder — all in one place.
rows.lead: Stock movements are atomic. Receive a batch, expiry and supplier are captured. Dispense, the system picks the closest-expiring batch. End of month, you have a Schedule-H register that’s ready for inspection.
bullets: FEFO dispensing prevents expired stock reaching the patient.
Schedule-H + Schedule-X compliance with regulator-ready register exports.
Multi-store transfers tracked end-to-end — no paper challan needed.

faqs.a: Schedule-X drugs have a separate dispensing path with prescriber verification and a printable register that matches the State drug authority’s format.

faqs.q: Can pharmacy run as a standalone for a separately-owned shop?
faqs.a: Yes — the pharmacy module can be enabled standalone for an attached but separately-billed pharmacy. The data flow stays clean across both ledgers.
